lines.text: of life. Understood on these lines, the beatitude would have
the same meaning as the words of Goethe: "Him who ever
manfully toils, we can redeem." In the Biblical context,
however, righteousness has a different sense; those are
praised as blessed whom God justifies, whom God acknow-
ledges, whom God accredits. The promise is addressed to
those who suffer not merely from the frailty and pain of
human life in general, but from their own sense of inferiority
and unworthiness. The reference is to those who are oppressed
by the feeling that they never can wholly be what they would
like to be, that neither before others nor before God can
they appear and present themselves as what in their deepest
being they truly are, that their essential being is always
neutralized by weakness and guilt, that they can never give
themselves as they really intend, and so always suffer from
the feeling of being misunderstood. In fact is there not in all
of us this yearning desire to be able to give clear and effective
expression to our essential being and our deepest will, to
stand forth in the sight of all and in God's sight as we feel
that we might be? Yes, this desire is latent in all men. Yet
often it is suppressed or distorted into a tense and nervous
striving to bring one's merit to light, to thrust oneself
forward by achievement or pose, by a convulsive effort to
make an impression on others, and in that impression to find
a mirror of one's true self.
Oh that we were freed from this urge! That we could
express ourselves spontaneously as we are! That our being
could unfold itself effectively and purely, and give a true
reflection of itself in the eyes of all! No doubt there is also
an attitude of resigned abandonment of effort, of contempt
for human judgments in general, the withdrawal of man into
himself in proud self-isolation from his fellows. And this
attitude may well suggest a certain strength of soul, and
compel our respect. But the beatitude is not meant for it.
Christ's blessing is addressed to those who wait for God
Himself to bestow upon them that for which they long, for
God to free them from the frustrations which shackle them,
